auth.step1note: Created once at oauth.yandex.ru. Its settings must list the Redirect URI exactly as shown above. Scopes: cloud_api:disk.read, cloud_api:disk.info, and cloud_api:disk.write — the last one only to delete rescued files from the cloud.

autopilot.title: Every couple of hours, re-check unavailable files and immediately download the ones that came back. Availability here changes faster than a full probe pass: on Oct 18, a fifth of the "available" files died within two hours, and 71 died between the probe and the download.

del.warn: This is irreversible. Deletion uses permanently=true, bypassing the Trash: files in the Trash keep occupying quota for 30 days, and the point of deleting is to free space. They cannot be restored afterwards.

hosts.how: You cannot pick a node when downloading: the Yandex API issues the link and chooses the machine itself. A repeated request sometimes returns a different one, so “try” asks for links again for this node or cluster. A cluster is a data centre; its state changes, and “not serving today” does not mean “never”.

loop.nothing: Nothing to download: everything selected is already on disk.
loop.title: Download on repeat
loop.why:
No probing: the download attempt is the check, and a truer one — it reads the whole file, not the first byte. The queue is rebuilt every round, so what is rescued drops out and rounds get shorter.

It will not end by itself: stop it with the job list's stop button.

mirror.how: Files are already on disk — nothing is copied: the program just learns about them and starts counting them in totals, tree and archives.

next.archive.lead: {n} {files} rescued, but in a single copy
next.archive.why: A 7z volume set is the second medium. Without it one disk failure takes everything rescued.
next.autopilot.done: Autopilot is on: it will recheck unavailable files and take back what returns.
next.autopilot.why: No need to press recheck by hand: autopilot walks them and takes back what returns.
next.busy.why: Wait for it to finish or stop it -- the next step appears then.
next.done.why: Everything is inventoried, checked and rescued. Come back later: availability shifts.
next.download.why: Availability is rotting: what serves today may not serve tomorrow.
next.loop.why: Unavailable files sometimes come back — missing ones less often. A pass takes about {hours} h.
next.probe.why: Until a file is checked there is no telling whether the server serves it at all.
next.scan.why: Until the cloud is fully inventoried, there is no seeing what exists and what is lost.
next.stale.why: Damaged datacentres come back in parts: yesterday's unavailable may serve today.
next.start.why: First it inventories the cloud: names, sizes, hashes and place in the tree. That is saved even for files that can no longer be downloaded.
